name: example — log in, then land on the thing under test
note: THE RULE THIS FILE EXISTS TO DEMONSTRATE: no credential is ever a literal here.
`requires` is checked at LOAD, before the browser opens, so a missing variable
costs you a second rather than a four-minute recording. A resolved value never
reaches a chapter label, the evidence JSON or the verdict table — the label
names the FIELD, never what went into it.
node scripts/check-flow.mjs flows/_example-login.json    # validate, no browser
PREFER NOT DOING THIS EVERY RUN. Logging in through the UI on every loop is slow
and makes every run depend on the login page still working. Do it ONCE with
--save-state, then use --state ./auth.json afterwards. This flow is for the first
run, and for when the login page itself is what you are testing.
Match strings are what a human READS on screen (a11y text), never refs — refs
shift per snapshot, and a pinned one would silently click the wrong element.
